audits.title: Managing antibiotics wisely: a quality improvement programme in a tertiary neonatal unit in the UK.
audits.standard: Reduce antibiotic usage rate by 20% of baseline by 31 December 2016
audits.setting: Tertiary neonatal unit, Abertawe Bro Morgannwg University Health Board, Swansea

cycle1.result: Baseline median antibiotic usage rate 347 per 1000 patient-days; antibiotics stopped within 36-48 hours in 32.5% of culture-negative sepsis screens.

audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary quality improvement programme with Vermont Oxford Network, shared strategies and PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic usage rate reduced to 198 per 1000 patient-days (43% reduction); stopping within 36-48 hours rose to 91%; antibiotic days per patient fell from median 3 to 2.

audits.other_findings: Annual mortality 5.5% and necrotising enterocolitis 1.4% for the VON cohort were the best recorded.
audits.citation: Makri V, Davies G, Cannell S, Willson K, Winterson L, Webb J, et al.. Managing antibiotics wisely: a quality improvement programme in a tertiary neonatal unit in the UK. BMJ Open Qual. 2018;7(2):e000285. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2017-000285. PMID: 29756072.

audits.title: Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing Practices for Neonatal Sepsis and Measurement of Outcome in New Born Unit at Kenyatta National Hospital.

cycle1.result: Appropriate antibiotics on admission in 313 (97.8%); not stopped at 48-72 hours in 148 (53.62%) who improved; blood cultures in 13 (4%).

audits.other_findings: Overall mortality 80 (25%); documentation poor; an admission checklist was recommended.
audits.citation: Tank PJ, Omar A, Musoke R. Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing Practices for Neonatal Sepsis and Measurement of Outcome in New Born Unit at Kenyatta National Hospital. Int J Pediatr. 2019;2019:7930238. doi:10.1155/2019/7930238. PMID: 31182965.

audits.title: Reducing Antibiotic Use in a Level III and Two Level II Neonatal Intensive Care Units Targeting Prescribing Practices for Both Early and Late-onset Sepsis: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Reduce antibiotics on admission, continuation beyond 72 hours and antibiotic utilisation rate by 28% each
audits.setting: One level III and two level II NICUs, Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, Hollywood, Florida

cycle1.result: Internal audit found antibiotics started in over 50% of admitted neonates, with variation in prescribing.

audits.intervention: Antibiotic stewardship programme with multidisciplinary team, sepsis evaluation tools and guidelines, universal early-onset sepsis calculator for ≥34 weeks, education and 48-hour discontinuation for culture-negative asymptomatic neonates.

cycle2.result: Antibiotics on admission fell 34.1%, continuation beyond 72 hours 45.3% and utilisation rate 34.9%.

audits.other_findings: Predetermined 28% goal exceeded for all three metrics.
audits.citation: Kahn DJ, Perkins BS, Barrette CE, Godin R. Reducing Antibiotic Use in a Level III and Two Level II Neonatal Intensive Care Units Targeting Prescribing Practices for Both Early and Late-onset Sepsis: A Quality Improvement Project. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2022;7(3):e555. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000555. PMID: 35720871.

audits.title: Audit to optimize antibiotics use in neonatal septicemia.
audits.standard: Appropriate antibiotic choice and dosing per prescribing protocols
audits.setting: Neonatal ward, tertiary care hospital, Lahore

cycle1.result: Optimum antibiotic dose prescribed in only 70.2%; 90.6% received cefotaxime and amikacin empirically.

audits.other_findings: Gram-negative bacilli in 81.2% of cultures; all 10 patients whose isolates were sensitive to empirical therapy survived.
audits.citation: Usman A, Khan MZ, Khan MZ, Hussain A. Audit to optimize antibiotics use in neonatal septicemia. Pak J Med Sci. 2022;38(6):1540-1545. doi:10.12669/pjms.38.6.5073. PMID: 35991235.

audits.title: Reduction of Vancomycin Use in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Professional recommendation to avoid empirical vancomycin in neonates without MRSA risk; aim 30% reduction in vancomycin AUR
audits.setting: Level-3 NICU, Joseph M. Sanzari Children's Hospital, Hackensack

cycle1.result: Mean vancomycin AUR 27 days of therapy per 1000 patient days.

audits.intervention: Provider education, clinical practice guideline and prospective audit with feedback via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Mean vancomycin AUR 17 days of therapy per 1000 patient days (37.1% reduction), sustained; guideline adherence 96%.

audits.other_findings: No drug-related morbidity or sepsis-related deaths; three neonates switched from oxacillin to vancomycin.
audits.citation: Bhavsar SM, Casella EB, Kim M, Lake P, Malik S, Philips K, et al.. Reduction of Vancomycin Use in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Project. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2025;10(3):e810. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000810. PMID: 40330428.

audits.title: Reducing Vancomycin Use in a Level IV NICU.
audits.standard: Aim to reduce vancomycin prescribing rate by 50% within 1 year and sustain for 1 year
audits.setting: 60-bed level IV NICU, academic referral centre (Children's National)

cycle1.result: 112 vancomycin days of therapy per 1000 patient-days, substantially higher than peer institutions.

audits.intervention: Physician education with benchmarking, pharmacy-initiated 48-hour antibiotic time-outs, clinical pathways for sepsis and NEC, and daily prospective audit with feedback.

cycle2.period: After 1 year, sustained for a further year
cycle2.result: 38 vancomycin days of therapy per 1000 patient-days (66% reduction).

audits.other_findings: Vancomycin-associated acute kidney injury fell from 1.4 to 0.1 events per 1000 patient-days.
audits.citation: Hamdy RF, Bhattarai S, Basu SK, Hahn A, Stone B, Sadler ED, et al.. Reducing Vancomycin Use in a Level IV NICU. Pediatrics. 2020;146(2):e20192963. doi:10.1542/peds.2019-2963. PMID: 32611807.

audits.title: A quality improvement initiative to reduce antibiotic use in transient tachypnea of the newborn.
audits.standard: Aim to reduce ampicillin and gentamicin days of therapy by 10% within 12 months in low-risk infants with TTN
audits.setting: Neonatal unit, NewYork Presbyterian-Weill Cornell Medicine

cycle1.result: 71% of infants with suspected TTN started on antibiotics.

audits.intervention: Evidence-based clinical pathway, admission huddles, and prescriber audit and feedback (Model for Improvement).

cycle2.result: Starting antibiotics fell sequentially from 71% to 41%, 13% and 0%; ampicillin use fell 26% and gentamicin 23%.

audits.citation: Senaldi L, Blatt L, Han JY, Gozum G, Venturini SL, Hauft S, et al.. A quality improvement initiative to reduce antibiotic use in transient tachypnea of the newborn. J Perinatol. 2024;44(1):119-124. doi:10.1038/s41372-023-01850-x. PMID: 38123798.

audits.title: Reducing Antibiotic Use for Culture-Negative Sepsis in a Level IV Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.standard: Unit Antibiotic Guidelines to reduce treatment of culture-negative sepsis
audits.setting: Level IV neonatal intensive care unit, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York

cycle1.result: Early-onset sepsis antibiotic DOTs 18.3/1000 patient days; overall unit DOTs 232.5/1000 patient days.

audits.intervention: Antibiotic guidelines, case audits, weekly antibiotic stewardship rounds and biweekly review of culture-negative sepsis cases at staff meetings (sequential PDSA cycles).

cycle2.result: Antibiotic DOTs for culture-negative sepsis fell 81%; early-onset sepsis DOTs 3.9/1000 patient days; overall unit DOTs 176.7/1000 patient days.

audits.other_findings: No change in balancing measures (initiation, re-initiation events, antibiotic spectrum index).
audits.citation: Lewis JM, Hodo LN, Duchon J, Juliano CE. Reducing Antibiotic Use for Culture-Negative Sepsis in a Level IV Neonatal Intensive Care Unit. Pediatrics. 2025;155(3):e2023065098. doi:10.1542/peds.2023-065098. PMID: 39999319.
